message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to individual university timetables, but I can give you a quick overview of what most Australian universities do around this time:

| Typical Academic Calendar | What Happens Around May |
|---------------------------|------------------------|
| **Semester 1** (most common system) | Starts mid‑February / early March → ends early June. Classes run Monday–Friday during weekdays, sometimes Saturday mornings for some programs. |
| **Summer Term / Short Courses** | Some schools offer short “summer” modules between April and August. These often start in late April or early May and finish in June or July. |
| **Intensive Workshops & Professional Development** | Many universities host intensive workshops, seminars, or certificate programmes throughout spring – especially in fields such as business, law, health sciences, and creative arts. |

### How to Find Specific Availability

1. **University Websites**  
   - Each major university in Sydney has its own online timetable portal:
     * [UNSW](https://www.unsw.edu.au/)
     * [UTS](https://www.uts.edu.au/)
     * [Macquarie University](https://www.mq.edu.au/) (though it’s technically just outside central Sydney)
     * [Western Sydney University](https://www.westernsydney.edu.au/)
     * [City, College of Law](https://www.citylaw.com.au/) (for professional legal training)

   Look under sections titled “Academic calendar”, “Course listings”, or “Student services”.

2. **Search Engines**  
   A simple Google query such as `"UNSW May 2025 courses"` will usually pull up the relevant page quickly.

3. **Contact Admissions Offices**  
   If you’re looking for something very specific—like a particular elective or a niche program—a phone call or email to the admissions office can confirm whether it’s scheduled for May.

4. **Online Course Platforms**  
   Universities increasingly use platforms like Canvas, Moodle, or Blackboard where students can view their personal enrolment status once logged in.

---

#### Quick Tips if You Want Something Right Now

* **Check the “Upcoming Events” section** on each university’s homepage—they’ll list open enrollment periods, orientation weeks, and key deadlines.
* **Look for “May 2025” in the search bar** on the site; many sites allow filtering by month/year.
* **If you’re interested in continuing education**, look for “Professional Development” or “Short Courses”; those tend to fill out more flexibly than full degree semesters.

Feel free to let me know which university(s) you're considering, and I can point you toward the exact pages where you’ll find the May timetable!
